gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much energy each station actually delivers at TV-sized AC loads. Michael Barton at techtest.org measured 623 Wh (81% of rated) from the BLUETTI AC70 and 366 Wh (71.5% of rated) from the EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max at a 50 W AC load, with the AC70 drawing about 8 W idle with an outlet on. ChatGPT's runtime calculator assumed a flat 85% usable for every station.
standout_why: I compared against the only cited rival page, bluettipower.com/products/ac70. It lists 'TV(65W) 8.2 Hours', which works out to about 533 Wh or 69% of 768 Wh, but it never states that percentage and gives no figure for any other brand. The EcoFlow FAQ (rank 1) gives only '500W (Surge 1000W)'. None of the result pages ChatGPT got gives usable AC Wh at low load or inverter idle draw for any station. CleanTechnica's C1000 Gen 2 test (Kyle Field) has no measurements. I'm scoring it 2 rather than 3 because techtest's units appear to be the German/EU versions, and the EcoFlow card ChatGPT showed is a 499 Wh RIVER 2 Max variant, not the 512 Wh unit that was tested.
decides: It changes the budget pick. At TV-sized loads the AC70 delivered 623 Wh against 366 Wh for the RIVER 2 Max, about 70% more energy, while ChatGPT's own cards price the two $50 apart ($359 vs $309; only the $359 is confirmed on bluettipower.com). For a 100 W TV that means roughly 6.2 h from the AC70 and about 3.7 h from the RIVER 2 Max. ChatGPT's 85% assumption gives about 4.3 h for the RIVER 2 Max, so it flatters the smaller EcoFlow most. On cycle life, Anker states its 4,000 cycles to 80% retention, but BLUETTI's AC70 page gives '3,000+' with no retention figure. So the normalised cycle-life column can only be filled for Anker.

findings.label: Measured usable energy at 50 W AC load
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC70: 768 Wh Powerstation mit USB-C, Solar-Ladeoption und LiFePO4-Akkus im Test (Michael Barton, techtest.org, 2024-12-29)
findings.note: Same test, other loads: 698 Wh at 250 W AC (91%), 707 Wh at 500 W AC (92%), 713 Wh over USB-C 100 W (93%). The article doesn't state the mains voltage; it is a German review, so probably the 230 V unit.

findings.label: Idle draw with an AC outlet on and no load
findings.note: Quote: 'Leerlauf-Stromverbrauch mit aktiver Steckdose, welcher auch bei +- 8 W liegt'. Against a 50 W TV, 8 W is about 16% overhead, which is why usable energy falls at low loads.

findings.label: Measured usable energy at 50 W / 150 W / 500 W AC load
findings.source_title: Test: ECOFLOW RIVER 2 MAX, fast perfekte Powerstation mit LiFePO4 Akku und 100W USB C (Michael Barton, techtest.org, 2022-11-16)
findings.note: USB-C 100 W gave 449.75 Wh (87.8%). The review gives a 3-6 W standby figure only with Wi-Fi and display on, not an AC-on idle figure. Tested unit is the 512 Wh model, probably the EU version.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy
findings.value: 850 Wh (83% of 1,024 Wh rated) at about 250 W continuous, 230 V
findings.source_title: Lighter, stronger and faster, but... Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 power station review (Marcus Schwarten, Notebookcheck, 2025-12-21, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: EU version, and not measured at a TV-sized load. The review says output was lower with fluctuating loads but gives no number. It reports no idle draw.

findings.label: Maker's own TV runtime and the efficiency it implies
findings.value: 8.2 h for a 65 W TV, about 533 Wh or 69% of 768 Wh
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC70 Portable Power Station | 1,000W 768Wh - BLUETTI US
findings.note: Arithmetic: 65 W × 8.2 h = 533 Wh; 533 / 768 = 69%. This is below ChatGPT's 85% assumption and below techtest's measured 81% at 50 W.
